standard.title: First Nations Australians' interconnections with Country/Place
standard.description: the ways First Nations Australians in different parts of Australia are interconnected with Country/Place
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y2 (AC9HS2K04): Students explained interconnections of First Nations Australians to a local Country/Place and the relationship between language, Country/Place and spirituality.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the diverse ways First Nations Australians in different parts of Australia are interconnected with Country/Place.

nodes.label: Multiple connections to Country/Place
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain that First Nations Australians can have connections to multiple Countries/Places and describe how these connections are formed.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain that First Nations Australians can have connections to more than one Country/Place and give at least one reason why.
nodes.typical_width: Explain that some First Nations Australians have connections to many Countries/Places through marriage, birth, parents, residence and chosen or forced movement; discuss how some people are connected to one Country because it is Mother's or Father's Country.
wider: Investigate how forced removal and the Stolen Generations disrupted Country/Place connections and what efforts are made to restore them
Explore how First Nations Australian people maintain connections to Country/Place when living away from it
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding multiple connection types is prerequisite to appreciating the diversity of interconnections across Australia — the next node requires this conceptual flexibility.

response_modes.reason: The concept of belonging to multiple Countries/Places challenges conventional notions of 'one home' — scaffold carefully using concrete examples from stories and community members.

success_criteria: Explains that a person can have connections to more than one Country/Place
Names at least two ways connections to Country/Place are formed (e.g. birth, marriage, residence)

nodes.label: Diverse expressions of connection
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore how First Nations Australians from different groups express their connections to Country/Place through poems, songs, paintings and stories.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one way a First Nations Australian group expresses their connection to Country/Place through an artistic or cultural form.
nodes.typical_width: Read and view poems, songs, paintings and stories from First Nations Australian groups outside the local area; discuss how these expressions reveal connection to Country/Place; compare expressions from different groups.
wider: Compare how two different First Nations Australian groups express connection to Country/Place and identify similarities and differences
Explore what these expressions reveal about the relationship between cultural practice and land

response_modes.reason: Engaging with expressions from multiple groups — not just the local group — broadens understanding of the diversity of First Nations Australian connections to Country/Place.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The diversity of First Nations Australian artistic expression of Country/Place connection is immense — engaging with multiple forms reveals both common themes and regional diversity.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one way a First Nations Australian group expresses connection to Country/Place
Describes what this expression reveals about the group's relationship with their Country/Place
